original.guitar: Jeff Lynne (lead and rhythm guitar); a 12-inch single lists a Gibson EDS-1275, Les Paul Custom and Marauder among his guitars
original.notes: Single from Secret Messages (June 1983), a 50s rock 'n' roll homage. Mik Kaminski plays the violin solo.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the Chuck Berry-style boogie rhythm (root-fifth to root-sixth shuffle on the low strings), channel B for a grittier sound. The piezo has a sharp attack, so pick a little softer than on the Tele, and palm-mute lightly. The 100 ms slapback is the 50s echo.
recipes.why: Same tweed-and-slapback recipe as the Tele version, adjusted for the piezo: less gain so it doesn't turn fizzy, treble and presence down and middle up to soften the quack, a light compressor for sustain, and more channel volume for the lower output. The guitar's EQ stays flat; all the shaping is on the Tonelab.
warnings: A piezo can't fully match the thick, punchy humbucker crunch on the record. It will sound brighter and lighter. That suits the boogie rhythm well, less so heavier parts.

original.guitar: Jeff Lynne; Gibson humbucker guitars (Les Paul Custom, EDS-1275) listed for the single
original.notes: Single from Secret Messages (June 1983). The main solo is on violin (Mik Kaminski).

recipes.tips: Channel A for Chuck Berry-style double-stop licks and fills, channel B for a solo. The main solo on the record is violin: if you cover it on guitar, use channel B. The compressor replaces the Tube OD from the Tele version, because extra overdrive on a piezo turns harsh. If it feeds back, drop COMP Sens to 3.
recipes.why: A JTM45-style crunch with the gain down a point from the Tele version, more middle and less treble and presence, so the piezo's double stops bite without fizz. The compressor gives the sustain the humbucker had naturally. The guitar's EQ stays flat; all the shaping is on the Tonelab.
warnings: A piezo can't fully match the thick humbucker lead sound on the record. Expect a brighter, more acoustic attack.
